requirement_trace.text: Existing Islamia operational ERP is a distinct current business implementation. Verify all existing operational modules, fix defects/security, and safely enhance them without changing valid data, historical location IDs, inventory/stock/finance semantics, owner and staff workflows.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Real core Islamia workflow regression (POS, purchase, stock, production, finance, permissions, reports), valid snapshot/backup and role/API tests before release; no unexpected behavior or history change.

requirement_trace.text: Central Owner platform and other business/industry modules not present in Islamia must be genuinely coded and integrated, not assumed from existing sweets-business code or declared ready because the Decision Book says approved.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Independent tenant + business setup, security, branding, role, API and E2E test for each required industry with clear built/partial/missing status; preserve sole repository and no shadow app.

requirement_trace.text: All Core 10 source and intended database changes originate as reviewed GitHub code, tested schema and versioned migrations; create a safe legacy production schema baseline before any new migration adoption; use staging and explicit approval for actual Supabase production changes. Verify migration history and drift after deployment.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Trace any live database object change to an exact reviewed SHA, migration file and approved deployment receipt; no untracked SQL hotfix, missing historical baseline, or claim Git push implicitly deploys.

requirement_trace.text: Claude and ChatGPT use shared repo-root instructions and one canonical GitHub-first protocol, plus an updated git-tracked CURRENT_HANDOFF.md. When usage ends, the next agent verifies latest PR branch SHA, CI, changed files, blockers, next exact action and Decision Book before continuing; agents must not concurrently overwrite one branch.
requirement_trace.acceptance: New agent can reproduce the actual development state from committed code, current GitHub PR/CI and a readable handoff; uncommitted work is never falsely assumed recoverable; verified coding progress not lost to separate chats.

requirement_trace.text: After actual code and role/regression testing, Claude Code must release small, safe, reversible frontend improvements to CORE-10-CENTRAL live website for the Owner's ongoing manual inspection, instead of indefinitely waiting for an entire ERP package. Follow verified GitHub Pages publishing process and provide owner-click smoke checklist and rollback.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Exact Git PR/SHA, applicable CI PASS, known deployment mechanism, changed live URL/version and smoke PASS; owner informed what to test. Sensitive SQL/RLS/RPC/stock/financial changes remain separately gated with real auth/staging/backup and explicit owner go/no-go.

requirement_trace.text: Owner may retain the universal Studio and independently place each supported control in Central only, selected Business App only, both, or hide from regular menus per business, and change placement later; apply separate business-specific setting values, edit delegation and approval policies without cloning authoritative controls or losing Owner discoverability.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Two businesses in the same tenant can display/configure same canonical control differently; independent tenant cannot see them. Owner can move/control both views; role/business permissions, session/RLS, change audit and approval are enforced on signed server APIs. UI projection and OFF/ON never independently grant writes.

requirement_trace.area: Universal Owner Control Studio / Reusable Micro-Engine Lifecycle
requirement_trace.text: Existing approved D033/A042 + D045 scope reaffirmed: the Owner has a permanently accessible cross-industry Universal Studio to configure all SUPPORTED safe operational controls (ON/OFF, visibility, role/user/site grants and explicit denial/expiry, approvals, rules/thresholds, notifications, automation/integrations); define/combine reusable small workflow, validator, calculator, report, rule, approval or automation/integration engine descriptors; version them and selectively make the SAME canonical control/engine available to one, several, or later different Business Apps, each with independent values, menu placement and delegated/request-only editing. Owner can revise/retract controlled configurations without programmer intervention where engine capabilities support it; new unsupported runtime code requires engineering and certification. No duplicated permission, storage, data, or history.
requirement_trace.authority: Owner explicit 2026-11-11; prior DISC-010/DISC-011 reaffirmed (not a new decision)
requirement_trace.acceptance: Acceptance: 1) Owner lists fixed AND newly registered eligible descriptors centrally, 2) creates/validates/version-controls a supported engine configuration, 3) chooses Business A/B independently with Central/Business/Both/Hidden placement, ON/OFF and scope-level values, 4) local Business Owner can edit only by delegated server authority or request approval, 5) effective-deny/signed RLS/Auth/tenant isolation and invariant gates, approvals, audit, stale version and config rollback tested, 6) never marks a descriptor operational before handler/finance/stock/security certified; 7) existing Islamia ERP unchanged.

requirement_trace.area: R124 implementation NOTE — C10-A045 first executable Micro-Engine slice (not a new requirement)
requirement_trace.text: Under existing Owner-approved R124, Workshop + one canonical multi-business engine distribution now have an executable FIRST SLICE (Draft PR #42). Registered threshold_rule_v1 advisory handler only, tested Business A/B independent publish/config and versioned site overrides. The 8 remaining engine types remain inert DRAFT/NOT IMPLEMENTED until handler certified. Configuration-only rollback does NOT roll back site overrides; those are separately versioned. Production SQL/GoTrue signed stages not done.
requirement_trace.authority: Claude implementation evidence 2026-11-11; informational note, NOT new Owner mandate/policy
requirement_trace.acceptance: Acceptance evidence: tested code SHA 9ac74519795a2ec7004da12a50d8e8859203405a, dedicated workflow #43003257646 SUCCESS. Existing R124 original text remains unchanged; Owner can still require remaining supported engines later. Do not claim engine types not built.

requirement_trace.area: Test Identities / Pre-Go-Live QA & Safe Replacement
requirement_trace.text: Owner gives standing permission to create and consistently reuse broad temporary DEMO staff/owner/role account profiles for ALL development tests without requesting actual personal Owner/Staff ID, including Master Owner, different Business Owners, Managers, Cashier, Factory/Branch Staff, Investor, Partner, Approver/Reviewer, Revoked, Unassigned, Software Operator, anonymous and unrelated tenant. Maintain a canonical alias/permissions/expected-scope register. For real signed tests use dedicated non-production GoTrue users in separate disposable stage with protected unique credentials and signed-token verification, never synthetic JWT in production. When deployment starts, deactivate/delete stage-only identities and data safely and use actual authorized users.
requirement_trace.authority: Owner explicit 2026-11-11; testing authorization, not unrestricted production identity creation
requirement_trace.acceptance: Acceptance: robust 2-tenant/2-business/4-site role matrix, stable IDs/aliases available to all agents and reused across E2E; staff actions and denials verified; stage-only GoTrue identities and live signed RLS/auth/revocation pass before certification; synthetic-only tests clearly labeled; no secrets in Git or production Supabase writes; demo logins and data safely removed before actual go-live without deleting real records.

requirement_trace.area: Demo-First End-to-End Structural Completion / Iterative Defect Register
requirement_trace.text: Build nearly the entire approved operational ERP structure and fully connected normal business workflows using reusable DEMO Owner/Staff identities and synthetic tenants/businesses/sites; do not wait for real personal credentials to implement POS, purchase, inventory, production, costing, finance, accounting, reports, audit, permissions, partner/owner features, templates and branch/factory/godown structures. Structural model must be usable, business-specific, cross-module consistent and not merely mocked, catalogued or documented. At go-live, noncritical defects discovered during early field use are tracked and fixed incrementally.
requirement_trace.authority: Owner explicit 2026-11-11 restatement (scope clarification, not new production authorization)
requirement_trace.acceptance: Acceptance: complete business/module/page/API/SQL/report matrix shows executable demo workflow and true status by module and role; 10 industry templates mapped with built vs missing, no fake readiness; 300+ site target remains separate measured readiness; blocked P0/security/correctness/recovery issues fixed before live, small UX/edge-case issues triaged by reproducibility/severity without hiding them; synthetic accounts eventually replaced/cleaned after signed staging.

requirement_trace.area: Build all three large ERP packages with safe future configurability
requirement_trace.text: A048+A049+A050 are ALL required, not alternatives. Design supported configurable Owner/Business/Site policy, workflow mode, thresholds, approvals and module/navigation layout on shared canonical tenant/business/stock data. Allow future certified rule/engine extensions without redesigning the whole ERP; arbitrary new features still need safe handler and tests.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Evidence must show connected inventory, purchase/production/sales/cost/report, Owner portfolio with demo users. Changes versioned/audited, permission/stock/finance invariants never disabled; status per handler not mocked, sensitive production auth gates preserved.

requirement_trace.area: MASTER ERP-WIDE Intent-to-Implementation + Explainable Guided UX / Recommendations / Safe Demo
requirement_trace.text: Across the ENTIRE ERP (all modules, industries, fields, roles, workflows, screens, calculations and reports), Owner can articulate desired behavior/output in ordinary language without knowing code, business mechanics, DB or calculation. Engineering must infer and map canonical context/data, business logic, formula/version, unit/currency/rounding/date, permissions, approvals, cross-module dependencies, UI placement, report generation, audit and QA. Supported certified owner-configurable options must work; unsupported/unknown must visibly enter a secure handler-build/validation/release workflow, not pretend to function. EVERY significant button/field/settings/report must include concise inline WHAT / WHEN / WHY / WHAT HAPPENS / WHERE RESULT SHOWN, typical recommended action and its reason, allowed exception route, permissions/risks, formula/data trace and where practicable safe demo/example/preview; at minimum clear instructions. Contextual Bangla+English, accessible mobile/desktop; per-business/site/role values derive from server. No uncontrolled arbitrary code/SQL, fake completed results or bypass of tenant/stock/finance/role/audit invariants.
requirement_trace.authority: Owner direct MASTER design requirement 2026-11-11. Cross-cutting mandatory on all new and existing supported features; additive to R124/R127, no production deployment authority.
requirement_trace.acceptance: Acceptance: capability graph + formal intent schema; certified handler and dependency/impact classifications; every feature metadata includes what/why/when/how/effect/normal recommendation/exception/example/result location/calculation trace and status; prove end-to-end two businesses and 4+ sites, role negative, stale/replay, unsupported handler blocked, report source reconciliation, safe examples/preview and locale/390px/1440px UX. GoTrue stage remains separate; app states NOT BUILT / CONFIGURABLE / NEEDS HANDLER / SOURCE TESTED / DEPLOYED truthfully. Detailed spec https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VNB-ub0V49fg1QAPqyALk-1P79eqgbHJZwAdbq5-mCg/edit

requirement_trace.area: Owner-controlled HR/Payroll rules and carry-forward — complete configurable engine
requirement_trace.text: Complete A054 ChatGPT-owned HR enhancement: configurable scoped direct/delegated HR+Reviewer+Payroll grants (or approval-based flow), fixed/% pay components with enable/off, effective-dated rates and tested calculation, overtime multiplier editable with explicit OFF option (1.00×=normal base rate, NOT 1%), configurable raw punch retention (36 months default adjustable with data-class/legal guards and dry-run), and cross-year annual leave carry-forward with balance/cap/expiry/audited reconciliation. Each has Owner-level guided UI, safe validation, reports, simulation/impact and verified server access; no new shadow payroll ledger, no finance payout.
requirement_trace.authority: Owner explicit 2026-11-11; does NOT approve any particular statutory/law-specific rate or retention purge
requirement_trace.acceptance: Acceptance: 2 tenant/3 business, Owner direct grant and delegated reviewer/expiry/revocation, policy history/versioning, OT factor compare 0/off/1/1.5 with legal guard and effective dates, custom percentage vs verified statutory distinction, 12–120 month existing setting clarified and safely extended if lawful, leave accrual/carry-forward/expiry/cap/cross-year approval; frozen payroll unchanged unless audited amendment; deny unauthorized edits; SQL+Node+Chromium CI and staging gate. Actual A054 build not yet done.

# CORE 10 Global Business Universe 2026

**Evidence date:** 2026-11-11. **Truth level:** research/specification, not implementation or legal certification. This is a representative global map, not an impossible census of every business.

## Operating models and canonical flow

CORE 10 must support B2C/D2C, B2B company-location accounts, wholesale/distribution/dealership, franchise, marketplace/B2B2C, subscription/preorder, project/contract, field service, rental, manufacturing/subcontracting, intercompany, agent/commission, agriculture and nonprofit/grant models. The reusable flow is:

`trigger → typed source document → scoped approval → domain event → stock/accounting/settlement effect → source-linked report → correction/reversal`

The commercial seller, inventory owner, physical custodian, fulfiller, invoice issuer, payment recipient and accounting entity are separate roles. A single `business_id` cannot safely collapse them for dropship, marketplace, franchise, consignment or intercompany work.

## Sector/workflow map

| Sector/model | Core workflow | Pack/adapter additions | Critical exceptions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Retail/wholesale | quote/order/POS → fulfil → invoice → settle → return | barcode, counter shift, price/promotion, channel mapping | oversell, split fulfilment, cash variance, no-receipt return |
| B2B/distribution | company-location account → quote → credit approval → delivery → AR | dealer programs, rebate/claim, territory | credit hold, sell-in vs sell-through, suspended location |
| Food/bakery | lot receipt → recipe batch → QC/release → transfer/sale | allergens, yield, expiry, recall | substitute lot, quarantine, waste, recall |
| Restaurant/cloud kitchen | order/check → KOT/KDS → serve/deliver → close | modifiers, table/session, rider/channel settlement | void after fire, split check, KDS outage |
| Paint/hardware | formula/shade → tint/QC → dealer sale | SDS/hazard adapter, PDC/cheque, principal scheme | retint, unsafe substitute, rebate dispute |
| Manufacturing | demand → plan → work order → issue → operations/QC → receipt | MES adapter, genealogy, capacity | rework, scrap, downtime, by-product, missing cost |
| Construction | bid/BOQ → commitment → site issue → progress acceptance → billing | BIM link, retention, change order | superseded drawing, disputed quantity, unapproved field work |
| Field service/maintenance | request → estimate/SLA → schedule/work order → evidence → invoice | asset history, meter, warranty | no access, repeat visit, emergency work, lockout |
| Import/export/3PL | contract → booking/documents → customs response → receipt/landed cost | country customs/LC/sanctions adapters | hold, demurrage, short shipment, amended documents |
| E-commerce/marketplace | listing/order webhook → reserve → fulfil → refund/reconcile | provider payout/fee adapter | replay, seller dispute, refund after payout |
| Rental/hospitality/real estate | reserve resource → dispatch/check-in/use → return/checkout | folio/night audit, lease, inspection | overbooking, damage, room move, early termination |
| Agriculture | field/season/activity → harvest lot → grade/aggregate → settlement | scheme/sustainability adapters | weather loss, mixed lots, offline producer capture |
| Nonprofit/NGO | award/restriction → budget/disbursement/expense → outcome report | IATI/donor export | restricted fund, in-kind gift, donor privacy |
| Healthcare/education/energy/public | ERP procurement/workforce/assets boundary | FHIR/OneRoster/

CIM/statutory adapters | consent, safety, privacy, appeal; research-only initially |

## Daily roles and operational controls

The minimum role universe is tenant owner, business owner, site manager, cashier/counter staff, requester, buyer, approver, receiver/QC, warehouse worker, planner/operator, maintenance technician, accountant/treasurer, HR/payroll, auditor, investor/partner, customer/contractor, revoked/unassigned user, anonymous attacker and platform operator without implicit tenant-data access.

At a small shop, one person may hold multiple roles through an explicit owner-approved compensating control. At 303 sites, policy-bounded local execution and exception queues replace a global approval bottleneck. Requester, approver, receiver, invoice verifier and payer remain separable.

## Universal failure chains

1. **Offline sale:** capture bounded intent → reconnect → reauthorize → revalidate price/tax/stock/period → accept/conflict/reject → one idempotent effect.
2. **Payment uncertainty:** timeout becomes `UNKNOWN` → inquiry/callback reconciliation → one settlement; retry never duplicates money.
3. **Transfer:** dispatch reduces source available and creates in-transit; receipt increases target; never revenue.
4. **Return:** inspect disposition → source-linked credit/refund → only resellable quantity returns to available stock.
5. **Tax/FX correction:** preserve original policy/rate evidence → correction document → balanced journal; missing policy/rate is incomplete, not zero.
6. **Disaster restore:** encrypted manifest → isolated restore → counts, stock lineage, ledger balance and audit reconciliation → separately approved cutover.

## Small-business versus enterprise counterexamples

- One mutable price works at one counter but fails across 303 sites; use versioned effective policy.
- A franchise outlet may look like a branch but be a separate legal operator; tenancy and intercompany cannot be inferred from branding.
- A quantity-only item works for simple resale but fails for serialized rental assets, expiring food, recall and custody.
- A central owner queue may feel safe but collapses throughput; route routine work locally and surface exceptions centrally.
- A donation is not a sale, a transfer is not revenue, payroll approval is not payment, and marketplace collection is not automatically platform revenue.

## Primary evidence

- Microsoft procurement/approval: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-how-use-approval-workflows
- Oracle procurement lifecycle: https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/procurement/26d/fapra/api-requisition-lifecycle-details.html
- Shopify B2B locations and purchase options: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/b2b/getting-started/terminology and https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/purchase-options
- GS1 traceability: https://support.gs1.org/support/solutions/articles/43000734475-how-does-traceability-work-
- ISA-95 ERP/MES boundary: https://www.isa.org/standards-and-publications/isa-standards/isa-95-standard
- UN/CEFACT trade standards: https://unece.org/trade/uncefact/mainstandards
- FAO traceability: https://www.fao.org/food-safety/food-control-systems/traceability---recalls/en
- WCAG 2.2: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/

All were retrieved 2026-11-11. Bangladesh tax, payroll, customs, retention and regulated-sector rules remain region-policy validation required.

## Deep workflow conclusions

1. Oracle/Business Central P2P: requisition→PO→receipt→invoice→payment requires partial-state lineage and matching.
2. SAP O2C: goods issue, billing and cash receipt are related but separate effects.
3. NetSuite intercompany: availability never silently authorizes cross-subsidiary fulfilment.
4. Workday hire: effective-dated assignment and policy snapshots matter; role title grants nothing.
5. Acumatica mobile warehouse: barcode commands need server validation and idempotency.
6. IFS/Epicor manufacturing: external workflow steps require compensation; API success is not atomic ERP success.
7. Salesforce quote/subscription: revenue orchestration remains bounded from canonical stock/GL.
8. Odoo/ERPNext P2P: modular inspection must not fork stock/AP.
9. ERPNext/MRPeasy MRP: missing cost must be incomplete, never zero-profit.
10. Shopify/Lightspeed: channel orders and returns require reconciliation to canonical locations.
11. Toast: restaurant KDS semantics extend shared sales/stock/settlement.
12. Jobber: field evidence and disputed completion need a mobile task journey.
13. Procore: drawing/RFI/change versions require immutable provenance.
14. OpenBoxes: lot/expiry/recall transfer to core;

clinical compliance does not.
15. Tally: voucher speed is useful; jurisdiction-specific tax cannot be copied.

## Verdict

Learn explicit scope, document lineage, role-oriented workspaces, typed reversals, mobile execution and governed extension. Do not imitate suite complexity, provider lock-in, license-gated core truth, fragmented per-app identities or a giant configuration UI. No reviewed vendor provides a free unlimited production stack.

# Adversarial Specialist Debate — Issue #68

**Executed:** ten real specialist subagents, in two waves, 2026-11-11. No fictional agents. A1–A4 and B1–B2 worked independently before C1/C2 cross-examination and D1/D2 repo reconciliation.

## Round 1 — independent positions

- **A1 Commercial/value chains:** separate seller, owner, custodian, fulfiller, issuer, recipient and accounting entity; agreements and reversals are shared infrastructure.
- **A2 Operations/roles:** task queues and local execution must coexist with maker-checker, stock conservation and explicit close/reconciliation.
- **A3 Verticals:** industry packs may add states/validation/views but cannot fork parties, sites, work orders, stock or journals; regulated sectors begin research-only.
- **A4 Risk/global:** locale is not jurisdiction; offline is bounded intent; approval binds payload; restore proof—not upload—is backup acceptance.
- **B1 Enterprise:** strongest pattern is scoped document lineage, role/data separation, effective-dated workflows and compensation for nontransactional adapters.
- **B2 Modular/vertical:** best UX is fast counter/mobile work plus deep reconciliation; “free/installed/connected” never proves zero-cost or operational readiness.
- **C1 Architect:** modular monolith, canonical stock/auth/approval/journal boundaries, additive bridges, no arbitrary Studio execution or automatic dual-write.
- **C2 UX/Operations:** task-led role workspaces, Quick/Advanced on one engine, BN/EN contextual guidance, visible pending/conflict/incomplete states and exception recovery.
- **D1 Repo forensic:** PR #7 exact head is green synthetic evidence; current PR #60 head is not all-green and differs from recorded green SHA; Claude namespaces and shared engines are protected.
- **D2 Data/security:** `org_scope_on` remains blocked; signed Auth is absent; `partner_calculate()` has an all-location business-scope defect; PR #27 owns integration ports.

## Round 2 — cross-examination

| Challenge | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Task verbs can hide quote/order/dispatch/invoice/payment effects | Task labels resolve to typed workflow steps with the next committed effect shown before execution. |
| Presentation descriptors can become a second policy engine | Descriptors name required capability only; server returns scope, decision, policy version, expiry and evidence. |
| Generic renderer is unsafe for cash close, count, payroll, production, settlement | Use renderer families and purpose-built typed high-risk components. |
| Central correctness can create a 303-site approval bottleneck | Execute routine work locally within policy; route immutable payload-bound exceptions to the narrowest authorized queue. |
| Offline usability can imply cached authority | Only `none`, `draft_only` or `bounded_intent`; reconnect reauthorizes and shows accepted/conflict/rejected. |
| Quick setup can hide consequential defaults | Version and expose defaults/blockers; Quick and Advanced submit the same canonical command. |
| KPI drilldown can still mislead | Include metric version, scope, time/currency basis, elimination policy, missing-source classes and reconciliation state. |
| Global search can leak tenant names/counts | Server-filter before results exist; context switch clears scoped caches. |
| Reversal button can ignore downstream consumption/settlement | Server supplies a typed reversal plan; UI previews it. |
| Research breadth could trigger duplicate engines | Registry retains breadth; build order

stabilizes shared posting/auth/trace contracts first. |

## Round 3 — joint resolution

Adopt one capability-rich modular backend and one context-simple task shell. Keep commercial documents, stock, accounting and settlement distinct. Use one stock book, one effective authorization service, one payload-bound approval service and one balanced source-linked posting boundary. Industry packs add typed fields/states/validation and task vocabulary without owning alternate ledgers.

The Presentation Contract is non-authoritative. It may drive placement, renderer type, semantic BN/EN guidance and result routes; it cannot contain grants, SQL/code, financial formulas, stock rules or secrets. High-risk journeys retain typed components.

The first safe slice is the deterministic synthetic demo factory: reuse A046 identities, generate two tenants/six businesses/303 sites, define stable A048/A049 expected commands, validate balanced expected math, negative cases and provenance, and never post. Drive follows only through PR #27 integration ports.

## Preserved dissent and unresolved gates

- C1 rejects a universal renderer or arbitrary write engine; C2 requires evidence to remain understandable to operators, not developer-only.
- PR #60 current-head failures/provenance must be resolved before reuse claims.
- Real signed GoTrue isolation, `org_scope_on`, partner calculation scoping, production migration/restore and paid/provider activation remain blocked.
- Claude A052–A057 work remains protected. A PR/work order is not proof of finished output.

**Registry result:** 116 source candidates → 32 unified capabilities; unexplained omissions: **0**.

# Unified Architecture Decisions

**Status:** proposed technical architecture under existing D030–D050/R123–R129; not a new Owner decision or release approval.

## Architecture verdict

Use a modular PostgreSQL-backed monolith now. Extract services only after measured contention or isolation need. Preserve:

`platform → tenant → legal entity → business → operating site → custody/stock location/device`

Bounded contexts own typed writes: Identity/Scope, Party, Catalog, Agreements, Commercial Documents, Fulfilment, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects/Work Orders, Workforce, Finance, Approval, Reporting, Integration and Audit.

## Decisions

| ID | Decision | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|
| UAD-001 | Reuse A018/A019 hierarchy and additive legacy crosswalk pattern | no rewrite of legacy PKs or mass FK migration |
| UAD-002 | One canonical stock quantity book evolving A018/A048 | packs cannot own balances/movements |
| UAD-003 | Separate order, fulfilment, invoice, journal and settlement events | stock movement never implies revenue/payment |
| UAD-004 | One typed double-entry posting boundary | DR=CR, source/version/currency/period/reversal required |
| UAD-005 | One effective authorization service compatible with A021/A034 | visibility/configuration never grants authority |
| UAD-006 | One typed approval/exception service | payload fingerprint and policy version bind approval |
| UAD-007 | Versioned effective configuration inheritance | invariant→tenant→business→site; explicit deny wins |
| UAD-008 | Industry packs are manifests plus typed extensions | no alternate party, permission, stock, journal or audit stores |
| UAD-009 | Immutable command/idempotency receipt plus outbox | guarantee one local effect; reconcile external outcomes |
| UAD-010 | Reports are source-linked read models | zero, missing, provisional and stale are distinct |
| UAD-011 | Strangler migration uses bridges and read comparison | no uncontrolled production dual-write |

Every mutation carries tenant/business/site, stable request ID, payload fingerprint, actor derived from signed session, expected version and typed command. # Google Drive Integration Contract

## Two separate requirements

1. **Project governance:** this repository reads/updates the existing CORE 10 Master Decision Book. It is not a product tenant integration and must never create a competing decision register.
2. **Product Drive adapter:** each tenant owner explicitly consents to narrowly scoped Drive document/export jobs. The platform owner's Google account is never blanket access to customer files.

## Current implementation truth

There is no product Drive adapter. PR #27 (`9da6403…`) owns provider accounts, secret references, dry-run, outbox/idempotency, retry lease, signature boundary, usage caps, audit and kill switch. Drive must extend/reconcile that contract; this Issue #68 branch deliberately does not create a second provider framework.

## Future adapter contract

`consent configured → scoped export request → queued → upload attempted → object/version verified → completed | conflict | retry | dead-letter | revoked`

Required fields include tenant/business/site, canonical source document/version, object purpose, approved folder mapping, MIME type, payload hash, idempotency key, expected ETag/version, token secret reference, requested/verified scopes, retry lease, quota usage, actor/correlation ID, retention and immutable audit result.

## OAuth and privacy

- OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with explicit tenant-owner consent and least scopes.
- Prefer app-created/app-visible files where product requirements permit; broader Drive access requires a specific reviewed need.
- Tokens are encrypted backend secrets referenced by ID; never browser-visible, logged, committed or stored in SQL metadata payloads.
- Platform operator has no implicit document access. Support access is separately consented, time-bound and audited.
- Revoke disconnects new jobs, invalidates token references and preserves nonsecret audit/provenance.

## Folder and object mapping

Mapping keys include tenant, business, optional site, document class and environment. User-selected folder IDs are validated within the consenting account. File names are display metadata, never authority. Cross-tenant folder/object IDs are denied without disclosing existence.

## Idempotency, conflict and quotas

- Same key/same payload returns the prior object/version; changed payload conflicts.
- Upload timeout remains `UNKNOWN` until query/reconciliation prevents duplicate objects.
- ETag/version mismatch becomes a visible conflict; no silent overwrite.
- Quota/rate-limit response schedules bounded backoff; owner sees usage/threshold and kill switch.

## Export versus backup

Invoices, receipts and reports are exports/attachments. A database file copied to Drive is still an **unverified backup**. Backup acceptance additionally requires encryption, complete manifest (DB/Auth/Storage/config as applicable), key recovery, isolated restore, counts/checksums, stock lineage, DR=CR reconciliation, tenant isolation and measured recovery evidence.

## Mock/stage/test plan

1. Reconcile PR #27 interfaces and add a `documents/drive` provider family.
2. Pure mock adapter with deterministic synthetic documents; no network/OAuth.
3. Test two tenants, revoked membership, cross-tenant object ID, duplicate retry, timeout-after-success, ETag conflict, quota, kill switch and secret redaction.
4. Explicitly authorized nonproduction OAuth stage using synthetic files.
5. Production connection only after privacy, rollback, monitoring and owner approval.

Official references (retrieved 2026-11-11): https://developers.google.com/drive/api/guides/about-auth and https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2

## 5. Cross-module invariants / business logic examples

- A purchase receipt creates an authorized **stock receipt** and proper AP/expense mapping where certified; it is not itself evidence of cash payment.
- Factory production has approved BOM/recipe, material issue, WIP and finished goods receipt; batch cost must reconcile, not fabricate wastage or margin.
- Branch/factory/warehouse transfer updates authorized locations without inflating consolidated sales/revenue. Same-business transfers ≠ sales.
- POS/online sale links customer/order, stock issue, revenue, cash/AR, tax if supported, COGS and transaction audit. Return/refund creates a bounded, source-linked reversal and fulfillment consequences.
- Payroll approved vs payroll paid vs bank disbursed are distinct states; no auto finance journal/payment without certified handler and authority.
- Customer refund/online checkout “success” requires signed provider event + amount/currency order match; retries must be idempotent.
- Investor, partnership, debt, capital/equity and fixed percentage obligations are distinct contracts; never call a hypothetical profit guaranteed or assign a false legal/sharia classification.
- Report “Net profit” requires complete sales + verified COGS + expenses + period/tax/adjustment basis; otherwise display \`INCOMPLETE\`, not a confident zero or invented percentage.
- Every relationship is scoped by tenant/business/site/location, effective date and authorization. A module's view must never auto-authorize an upstream mutation.
- Balanced journal \`sum(debit) == sum(credit)\`, source-event idempotency, undo via reversal, conserved stock moves, exact units and rounding, immutable posted history.
- Contextual help must explain expected effects (“what changes

now / what does not change”), dependencies and report destination. Offer safe demo before real changes.

# C10-A051 — Multi-business Workforce, Attendance, Leave & Payroll Engine
Status: **BUILT and isolated-CI tested (disposable `c10_demo`)**. NOT applied to IMG-ERP-SG, NOT real-GoTrue tested, NOT released.
Owner of this package: Claude (new `c10_a051_*` / `core10-workforce-*` files only). Draft PR, never merged to `main`.

## 1. What exists (real code)
| Layer | Files |
|---|---|
| SQL (apply in order, after A018) | `internal/enterprise-sql/c10_a051_workforce_core_v1.sql`, `..._attendance_leave_v1.sql`, `..._payroll_v1.sql`, `..._reads_v1.sql` |
| Signed API client | `core10-workforce-client.js` (strict allow-list of 49 RPCs, argument typing, `auth.getUser()` each call, `schema('c10_demo').rpc`) |
| UI (390px mobile + 1440px desktop) | `core10-workforce-{directory,attendance,leave,payroll,reports,self}.html`, `core10-workforce-app.js`, `core10-workforce.css` |
| Tests | `tests/c10_a051_workforce_e2e.sql` (PG), `..._concurrency.sh` (parallel sessions), `..._client.test.js`, `tests/api/core10-a051-workforce-rest-e2e.js` (signed HMAC → PostgREST), `tests/e2e/core10-a051-workforce-browser.js` (Chromium) |
| CI | `.github/workflows/core10-a051-workforce-ci.yml` |

Flow for every feature: **UI → signed `auth.getUser()` client → `c10_demo.wf_*_v1` SECURITY DEFINER RPC → business rules + DB-derived authority → deterministic calculation → append-only hash-chained audit → reports/exports.**

## 2. Reuse, not duplication
* Identity/tenancy: only existing `c10_demo.tenants / businesses / sites / tenant_members / business_members` and `can_tenant()`. **No new login, no new site_grants, no new role table.** An optional `wf_employees.user_id` link (owner-created) gives *self-service only*.
* No finance ledger, stock movement, bank file or payout. "Approved/Frozen" ≠ "Paid" (`paid:false`, `money_movement:false`, `ledger_posted:false` in every contract response; payslip says `payment_status: not_tracked_in_this_module`).
* Legacy `employees.js / attendance.js / shifts.js / salary.js / payroll.js / staffreports.js / v2/**` are untouched (git diff shows only new A051 files). No real staff data is read or migrated.

## 3. Authority model (server-derived on every call; claims/JWT metadata are ignored)
| Persona (A018 fixture id) | Workforce authority |
|---|---|
| Tenant owner (1111…) | everything in own tenant incl. payroll; may loosen maker-checker; may activate statutory components; retention purge |
| Business owner (2222…) | everything in own business incl. payroll (cannot loosen maker-checker, cannot activate statutory components, no purge) |
| Manager (3333…) | directory (no PII/salary), shift roster, punch import, OT decisions, leave review (setting `leave_review_level`), reports/exports (masked names). **No payroll, no salary, no employee edit unless owner enables `manager_can_edit_employees`** |
| Supervisor (employee flagged `is_supervisor`, a1…) | own-site staff attendance, punch import for own site (not own punches), correction **requests** (never self, never approve) |
| Employee (linked user a2…/a3…/a6…) | own attendance, own leave (request/cancel), own limited payslip (frozen only), own advance request |
| Stock-only site staff (4444… before link), investor (5555…), revoked manager (6666…), other-tenant owner/staff (7777…/8888…), platform operator (9999…), anon | **denied** (`wf_denied` / permission denied). `stock.read/post` never implies workforce access |

Maker-checker (default ON): payroll preparer cannot review or approve; correction/le

ave/advance approver ≠ requester; nobody approves their own attendance/leave. Only the tenant owner can turn maker-checker off.

## 4. Data model (all tables RLS-on, zero direct grants)
`wf_business_settings, wf_departments, wf_employees, wf_employment_history*, wf_assignments*, wf_shifts, wf_shift_assignments*, wf_holidays, wf_punches†, wf_attendance_days, wf_attendance_corrections, wf_overtime_approvals*, wf_leave_types, wf_leave_requests, wf_pay_policies, wf_salary_structures*, wf_pay_components, wf_employee_components*, wf_advances, wf_advance_recoveries*, wf_payroll_runs, wf_payroll_lines, wf_payslips*, wf_receipts*, wf_audit*`
`*` append-only (trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE even for table owner). `†` immutable except the tenant-owner retention purge. Runs/lines freeze after review (`wf_frozen_payroll_immutable`). Effective-dated facts use "latest `effective_from ≤ date`" so history is never rewritten. Audit is a per-business SHA-256 hash chain verified by `wf_integrity_report_v1`.

## 5. Calculation rules (all deterministic `numeric`, Asia/Dhaka)
* **Day (derived from immutable punches + approved corrections/leave/OT):** work date = shift start date (overnight 22:00→06:00 supported; punch window start−3h … end+3h); duplicate punches within `duplicate_window_seconds` or same device ref are ignored; worked = out−in−break; late if in > start+grace; OT only after shift end ≥ `min_overtime_minutes`, capped by `max_overtime_minutes_per_day`; work on weekly-off/holiday = off-day OT; worked < `half_day_ratio`×scheduled ⇒ `half_day`; missing in/out ⇒ `incomplete` (blocks payroll); no punch on a scheduled day ⇒ `absent`.
* **Overtime** is paid only for minutes approved by a manager/owner (default; `overtime_requires_approval`).
* **Monthly:** `basic = base × employed_days / calendar_days`; day rate = `base / (monthly_divisor ∨ calendar_days)`; absence deduction = (absent + unpaid leave + ½ half-days + ⌊late_days / late_to_absent_days⌋) × day rate, **capped at basic**; hourly rate = day rate / standard hours. **Daily:** `base × (present + ½ half + paid leave*)`. **Hourly:** `base × regular hours`. (`*` configurable). OT = hourly rate × approved hours × multiplier (separate weekday / off-day multipliers, **default 1.00 – no statutory rate is asserted**).
* **Components:** allowances/deductions fixed or % of basic, per-employee assignment/override, optional proration. **Statutory components are created `pending_owner_approval` (OFF) and only the tenant owner can activate them.**
* **Advances:** approval creates a *deduction schedule only*; recovery = min(installment, remaining, headroom). Recovery rows are written only at FREEZE (amendment-safe).
* **Net = gross − deductions, never negative** (`CHECK(net>=0 AND net=gross−total_deductions)`; deductions/recoveries are capped with warnings).
* Rounding: `half_up` or `down` to 2 dp per component; money limits ≤ 99,999,999,999.99.
* Worked fixture (October 2026, EMP-001): base 31,000; 21 present, 1 half, 1 absent, 1 unpaid + 2 paid leave, 3 late days (→1 day), OT 60 min weekday + 420 min weekly-off at ×2.00 = 2,000; allowances 1,000 + 10 % = 4,100; gross 37,100; deductions 3,500 + 200 + 1,000 advance; **net 32,400** (asserted in the e2e).

## 6. Payroll lifecycle
`preview (not stored) → DRAFT → REVIEWED → APPROVED → FROZEN` (+ `return_to_draft`, `void`). Blocking exceptions (no salary structure, incomplete attendance, pending OT/leave/correction, period not ended) must be resolved and the draft reca

lculated; review/approve/freeze re-compute an input hash and refuse stale drafts (`wf_payroll_inputs_changed`). Reviewed/approved/frozen periods lock attendance corrections, punch import, holidays, employment/assignment/shift changes and leave. A frozen period can only change through an **audited amendment draft** (reason ≥ 10 chars) that supersedes (never rewrites) the original; employees keep both payslips and v1 is flagged `superseded`. Freeze issues immutable payslips (employee sees only their own limited payslip).

## 7. Reports / exports / controls
Attendance summary by site, headcount (site/status/contract), payroll gross/net by site, frozen payslip register, CSV exports (`employees`, `attendance`, `payslip_register`) with PII-safe role projection (no phone/NID ever; managers get masked names; formula-injection neutralised; every export audited), integrity report (audit chain, frozen totals vs lines, payslip per line, no negative net, one frozen run per period, advance not over-recovered), audit list, retention preview/purge for expired punches (tenant owner, never inside locked/frozen periods).

## 8. Integration contract (read-only; for A050 Portfolio / future finance)
* `c10_demo.read_workforce_business_summary_v1(p_business bigint, p_period date)` → active headcount, by-site headcount, frozen payroll totals; owner-level only.
* `c10_demo.read_payroll_liability_preview_v1(p_business bigint, p_period date)` → `state: approved_not_paid | no_approved_run`, gross/deductions/net preview; always `paid:false, money_movement:false, ledger_posted:false`.
* Future finance posting must consume the **frozen run id** and own its own ledger/payout; A051 will not write any money movement. Navigation: expose routes `core10-workforce-*.html?biz=<id>`; `owner.html`/`index.html` are intentionally not edited.
* Persona keys: this branch uses the A018 fixture UUIDs plus six inert employee ids (a1…, a2…, a3…, a5…, a6…, c2…). Re-map to A046 persona aliases when PR #44 lands (data-only change in `tests/c10_a051_workforce_seed.sql`).

## 9. Known limitations / NOT VERIFIED
* **Real Supabase GoTrue-issued session verification: NOT RUN** (release gate). CI uses signed-claim simulation + HMAC PostgREST.
* **Live SG migration: NOT APPLIED** (and not authorised). Real staging: not available → NOT VERIFIED.
* Single-day granularity only: no half-day leave, no multi-year leave carry-forward/cross-year requests, no per-employee weekly-off override beyond shift.
* Employee-change effective dates for employment status are limited to ≤ today (documented mirror semantics).
* Live attendance calculation is capped (35-day list, 92-day report, 1000 employees/run); very large tenants need the stored timesheet path + indexing review.
* Taxes, provident fund, bonuses, bank/MFS payout files and statutory rates are **not implemented by design** (components exist but statutory ones stay OFF).
* Browser UI is tested with a synthetic fixture; DB behaviour is tested separately through SQL and HTTP.
* Delegated HR/reviewer role: no existing delegated-permission contract was found on this base → payroll **fails closed to owners**.

# C10-A053 + C10-A054 — Workforce Integration & Payroll/Leave Governance
Status: **BUILT and isolated-CI tested (disposable PostgreSQL, synthetic A046 personas)**. NOT applied to IMG-ERP-SG, **real GoTrue NOT tested**, not released. Draft PR #63, never merged to `main`.
Reuses A018 identity, A046 personas, A050 Portfolio and the **unchanged A051 engine**; adds only `c10_a053_*` / `c10_a054_*` SQL, `core10-workforce-{integration,delegation,policy,liability}.html`, `core10-workforce-policy-{app,client}.js|css` and tests.

## 1. Files
| Layer | Files |
|---|---|
| SQL (apply after A051, in order) | `c10_a054_workforce_policy_v1.sql`, `c10_a054_workforce_bridge_v1.sql`, `c10_a053_workforce_integration_v1.sql` (A053 also loads **without** A051/A054) |
| Client / UI | `core10-workforce-policy-client.js` (strict allow-list of 25 RPCs), 4 pages, `core10-workforce-policy-app.js`, `core10-workforce-policy.css` (English + Bangla, 390px / 1440px) |
| Tests | `tests/c10_a054_policy_e2e.sql`, `c10_a053_integration_e2e.sql`, `c10_a053_not_connected_e2e.sql`, `c10_a054_concurrency.sh`, `c10_a054_regression.sh` (A051 e2e with hooks), `c10_a053_a054_client.test.js`, `tests/api/core10-a053-a054-workforce-rest-e2e.js`, `tests/e2e/core10-a053-a054-workforce-browser.js`, stack builder `c10_a053_stack.sh` |
| CI | `.github/workflows/core10-a053-a054-workforce-policy-ci.yml` |

## 2. Approval is NOT payment (hard rule)
* A051 `approved` / `frozen` only fix the **amount owed**. There is no function that pays, creates a bank file, moves money or posts a ledger entry (a Node test fails the build if such an API name appears).
* `a054_payment_records` holds **records of payments made outside the system** (`external_payment_record` / `reversal`, append-only, external reference required, never more than the outstanding approved amount, per-employee/month). Every response carries `payment_executed:false, money_movement:false, ledger_posted:false`.
* Per employee-month state: `approved_unpaid` → `partially_paid_recorded` → `paid_recorded` (+ `overpaid_recorded` flagged). Draft/reviewed runs are reported only as a *pre-approval estimate*, never as liability.
* `a054_liability_report_v1` shows **approved-unpaid, partly-paid-outstanding, recorded-paid and total outstanding as separate figures**, by site and by employee number (no names), plus a PII-safe, audited CSV. UI buttons are labelled "Approve amount owed (does NOT pay anyone)" and "Record payment made outside…".

## 3. A053 — integration
* **Persona registry** `a053_persona_registry`: the 16 A046 personas (alias == A046 key, UUIDs unchanged; a Node test compares SQL to the manifest) + 9 `A051_FIXTURE_ONLY` aliases for A051-only identities (a1…, b1…, b2…, c1…, c2…). Append-only trigger: an alias can never be re-pointed (no silent UUID reassignment). Unknown alias ⇒ `a053_alias_unmapped` (fail-closed). `a053_a051_alias_map` maps the 18 A051 short names.
* **Staff identity** (owner-only): `a053_link_staff_identity_v1` links an employee to a *registered alias* (never a raw UUID). Refused: unknown alias, platform operator / investor / revoked / partner (not linkable), other tenant, other business scope, employee or login already linked. A link grants **self-service only**; unlink is immediate. `a053_staff_overview_v1` (manager+; aliases owner-only, names masked for managers), `a053_my_assignments_v1` (self).
* **Owner Portfolio → Workforce adapter** `a053_read_portfolio_workforce_v1(period)`: per business visible throug

h A050; **owner-level only** per business. Every figure comes from A051's server guards (`read_workforce_business_summary_v1`, `read_payroll_liability_preview_v1`) and is verified (business id, month, headcount = sum of sites, `paid/ledger_posted/money_movement = false`) — otherwise `CONTRACT_VIOLATION` and no figures. Managers, investors, site staff get `OWNER_ONLY` with no data; other tenants never appear. Missing A051 ⇒ `NOT_CONNECTED`, no numbers invented.

## 4. A054 — governance
| Feature | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Delegated roles | `a054_delegations`: `hr`, `payroll_preparer`, `payroll_reviewer`, `payroll_approver`, `payment_recorder`; business / site (HR only) / month-period scope; explicit **DENY beats ALLOW**; expiry; revoke. Evaluated **live on every call** (clock_timestamp) so revocation/expiry bite on the next call, including calls already queued behind the per-business lock (tested with real parallel sessions). Delegate must be an active manager/owner or linked employee; owners cannot self-delegate; delegates cannot delegate. |
| Maker-checker | preparer ≠ reviewer ≠ approver for delegates; an employee inside a run cannot decide it; owners keep A051 semantics; `void` stays owner-only. |
| Effective-dated policies | `a054_policy_versions` (immutable, versioned): `overtime`, `pay_rule`, `leave`. Payroll policies start on the 1st of a month; leave policies on 1 Jan. A version cannot start inside a period that is reviewed/approved/frozen (or a leave type with requests) → `a054_effective_date_locked`. |
| Overtime | multiplier semantics **1.00× = 100% of base hourly rate (not 1%)**; <1.00 → `a054_multiplier_below_base_rate`, >5.00 → `…_use_x_not_percent`. **OFF mode** needs the *tenant owner* + a legal-review reference. No statutory rate is shipped; with no policy row A051 behaviour is untouched. |
| Allowance / deduction rules | fixed or percent (percent units: 10 = 10%) of `basic_earned` / `gross_before_rule` / `contract_base`, min/cap, scope by contract type / site, proration, **per-line trace** (base, base value, raw, cap, policy version). Statutory rules need tenant owner + legal reference. Codes may not collide with A051 components. |
| Leave | accrual (`upfront` / `monthly`), annual **carry-forward with cap**, **expiry months + grace days** (carried days are consumed first and forfeited after expiry), **cross-year requests** (days counted per year), balance read incl. next-year carry preview. Quota is enforced inside A051 `request_leave` / `decide_leave` (hooked). |
| Retention | raw punches only (36-month default setting kept); **legal holds** (owner places, tenant owner releases) protect punches from A051 purge; dry-run report; payslips, runs, leave and audit are never purged. |
| Audit / idempotency | every write uses A051's request-key receipts and hash-chained `wf_audit` (integrity report stays green). |

### Honest note on the A051 hooks
`c10_a054_workforce_bridge_v1.sql` rewrites **one exact statement** in each of 12 installed A051 functions via `pg_get_functiondef()` (22 hooks; install fails closed if a statement is missing/ambiguous; logged in `a054_patch_log`). A051 source files are untouched. With no A054 data every hook is a no-op: `tests/c10_a054_regression.sh` runs the **unchanged A051 e2e + concurrency** on a database with A054 installed. Hooked: payroll OT + rule engine (`wfi_calc_line`), preview/draft/recalculate/transition, payroll run reads, leave decide/request, correction decide, employee edit, punch

purge.

## 5. Privacy / authorization summary
Staff see only their own payslip/leave/assignments; no salary, liability, policy, delegation or retention data. Investors, revoked, platform operator, unassigned/partner users, other-tenant owners and anon are denied (`wf_denied` / permission denied). All new tables are RLS-on with zero grants; helpers `a05[34]i_*` are not executable by `authenticated`.

## 6. Not verified / limits
* **GoTrue NOT tested**; no staging; no production; CI uses signed-claim simulation + HMAC PostgREST + a synthetic browser fixture.
* HR delegation covers leave decisions, correction decisions and employee edits; roster, shifts and attendance import remain A051 manager rules. Site-scoped delegations are HR-only. Policy periods are month/year aligned (no mid-month proration of a policy change).
* Leave simulation is per employee/type/year (bounded recursion ≤10 years); very large tenants need review. Single-day granularity (no half-day leave) is inherited from A051.
* The REST e2e (`tests/api/core10-a053-a054-workforce-rest-e2e.js`) needs Docker/PostgREST and is verified only in GitHub Actions.
* No bank/MFS payout, tax, provident fund, bonus or statutory rate is implemented.

# C10-A055 — Enterprise Assets & Maintenance: RPC contract (authoritative)

Schema `c10_demo` (disposable only). Public API = `am_*_v1` / `read_asset_maintenance_business_summary_v1`, all
`SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path=c10_demo,pg_catalog`, `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO authenticated` only (lockdown file).
Internal helpers `ami_*` are NOT executable by `authenticated`/`anon`. Direct table access is revoked.

## Conventions
* **Writes**: `(p_business bigint, p_request text, ...)` → `jsonb` containing `status` (`applied` / `replayed` is transparent: a replay
  returns the *original* receipt). Begin with `ami_begin`, finish with `ami_finish`, audit with `ami_log`.
  Request key `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,100}$`; same key + different payload/actor/op → `am_idempotency_conflict`.
  Per-business serialisation: `ami_begin` takes `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on `businesses` after authorising.
* **Reads**: `(p_business bigint, ...)` → `jsonb`, STABLE, use `ami_read_ctx`; never insert rows. Lists → `{items:[...],total:n}`.
* **Optimistic concurrency**: mutable rows carry `version`; updates take `p_expected_version`, else `am_stale_version`.
* **Errors** (stable `RAISE EXCEPTION '<code>'`): `am_denied` (outsider / revoked / other tenant — also for hidden entities),
  `am_not_permitted` (member lacking capability at that site), `am_owner_required`, `am_invalid_input`, `am_stale_version`,
  `am_idempotency_conflict`, `am_invalid_request_key`, plus specific `am_*` codes documented per RPC.
* **Authority** comes only from DB state (`ami_ctx`). JWT claims/roles never elevate. Capabilities per role: see `ami_role_caps`.
  `ami_has(c,site,cap)` / `ami_need_cap(c,site,cap)`; owners = tenant owner or business_owner.
* **Policy** via `ami_cfg_*(business, site, category, key)` (category > site > business > default). Keys: `am_policy_catalog`.
* **No side effects outside module**: no stock, ledger, payroll or purchase writes. Money fields are ADVISORY.
* JSON keys are snake_case = column names unless noted. Timestamps ISO-8601 (timestamptz), dates `YYYY-MM-DD`.

## File ownership / load order
`core` (tables, helpers, policy catalog, audit) → `policy` → `registry` → `planning` → `workorders` → `reports` → `lockdown`.
Cross-file internals (plpgsql, so definition order is not validated, but names/signatures are fixed here):
* `ami_create_wo(c am_ctx_t, p_request text, p_asset bigint, p_kind text, p_title text, p_description text, p_priority text,
   p_source text, p_target bigint, p_due date, p_checklist_code text, p_extra jsonb) RETURNS bigint` — owned by **planning**;
  inserts the work order (status `DRAFT`, or `SUBMITTED` when `p_extra->>'submit'='true'`), numbers it, computes SLA due times from policy,
  snapshots the active checklist template into `am_wo_checklist`, writes the `am_wo_history` row; no audit/receipt (caller does).
* `ami_complete_target(p_target bigint, p_done_on date, p_reading numeric) RETURNS void` — owned by **planning**; re-anchors the plan
  target (`last_done_*`, `next_due_*` by policy `schedule.anchor`/plan anchor), called by workorders on completion of plan-sourced WOs.

## policy file (core owner)
`am_whoami_v1(p_business)` · `am_policy_catalog_v1(p_business)` · `am_get_policy_v1(p_business,p_site,p_category)` ·
`am_save_policy_v1(p_business,p_request,p_expected_rev,p_scope_type,p_scope_id,p_changes jsonb,p_reason)` ·
`am_reset_policy_v1(p_business,p_request,p_expected_rev,p_scope_type,p_scope_id,p_keys text[],p_reason)` ·
`am_apply_preset_v1(p_business,

p_request,p_expected_rev,p_preset,p_scope_type,p_scope_id,p_reason)` ·
`am_preview_policy_v1(p_business,p_scope_type,p_scope_id,p_changes jsonb)` (simulation, no writes) ·
`am_simulate_schedule_v1(p_business,p_params jsonb)` (pure) · `am_policy_history_v1(p_business,p_limit)` · `am_bootstrap_v1(p_business,p_request)`.

## registry file
Writes: `am_grant_role_v1(p_business,p_request,p_user uuid,p_role,p_site bigint,p_note,p_reason)` (owner) ·
`am_revoke_role_v1(p_business,p_request,p_grant bigint,p_reason)` (owner) ·
`am_save_category_v1(p_business,p_request,p_id,p_expected_version,p_data jsonb,p_reason)` (owner) ·
`am_save_code_v1(p_business,p_request,p_kind,p_code,p_label,p_label_bn,p_active,p_reason)` (owner) ·

# C10-A056 Universal CRM, Customer Lifecycle & Sales Integration

Status: DRAFT source build, disposable PostgreSQL only (PR #66). Not production, not GoTrue-verified, no real messaging, no real finance.
Namespace: everything is `a056_*` in schema `c10_demo` (files `internal/enterprise-sql/c10_a056_{core,pipeline,growth}_v1.sql`).
Legacy Islamiya `crm_*.js`, `customers.js`, `website.js` are untouched and are NOT the source of this module.

## Canonical dependencies (reuse, never duplicate)
| Dependency | How A056 uses it |
|---|---|
| A018/A019 tenancy (`actor_uid`, `can_manage`, `can_business`, `can_site`, `can_see_business`) | Single authorization root; checked live on every call, so role revocation is immediate. No second permission system. |
| A049 `create_operation_order_v1`, `read_operation_overview_v1` | The ONLY order integration. Accepted quotation lines become A049 **draft** `sale_issue` orders; fulfilment/posted state is read back via the overview contract. A056 never writes A049/A048 tables (CI asserts the SQL contains no such statements). Confirm/post stay in A049. |
| A047 sites / A046 personas | Site-scoped rows (`site_id`) use A018 site grants. Tests use A046-compatible synthetic UUIDs. |
| A022 / finance read models | No certified customer-receivable read model exists in the repo. A056 exposes a **registry** (`a056_register_finance_source_v1`, Owner only) and shows `NOT_CERTIFIED` / `UNAVAILABLE` / `RESTRICTED` with `null` balances until an Owner registers a certified function. |
| A050 | Same conventions (idempotency keys, versioned writes, signed client). |

Load order: A018 backend + seed, A020, A018 inventory, A048, A049, A050, then `c10_a056_core_v1.sql`, `c10_a056_pipeline_v1.sql`, `c10_a056_growth_v1.sql`. Rollback: drop the `a056_*` tables/functions (additive; nothing else references them).

## Verified journey (tests/c10_a056_crm_lifecycle_e2e.sql)
Lead -> Enquiry -> Opportunity -> versioned Quotation (approval rule, self-approval blocked) -> accepted -> A049 draft order (owner) -> confirm/post in A049 (stock) -> Purchase history/fulfilment `posted` -> Won (only after order) -> Invoice/Payment status (NOT_CERTIFIED until registered) -> Ticket/SLA/resolution evidence -> Follow-ups -> Campaign (consent-aware, NO-OP) -> Reports (dashboard, funnel, retention, repeat business, follow-ups, tickets).

## Design rules
- **Tenancy/RLS**: every table is tenant+business(+site) scoped with RLS enabled; `authenticated` has SELECT-only through row policies (site staff see only their sites), **no** INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; idempotency, suppression and intake-token tables have no direct grant. All writes go through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that re-derive authorization. Internal helpers are not executable by `authenticated`/`anon`.
- **Action tiers** (owner/manager/site) come from the versioned, Owner-editable config (stages, permissions, approval rules, SLA, loyalty, intake limits). Invariants cannot be weakened: `settings.write`, `customer.redact`, `finance.register` stay Owner; consent/opt-out and certified-finance rules are not configurable. Module is OFF until an Owner enables it. "Site tier" = any active A018 site grant for that site (the grant model has no CRM-specific actions yet; documented limitation).
- **Idempotency & concurrency**: every write takes a request key (replay returns the original receipt, conflicting reuse fails); advisory lock per key; `FOR UPDATE` + expected versions for merge, quotation revision, stage mov

es, tickets. `tests/c10_a056_concurrency.sh` proves one-winner behaviour with real parallel sessions.
- **Audit**: append-only `a056_audit` (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE blocked by trigger); settings history keeps every config version.
- **Customers**: tenant/business customer + organization/contacts, duplicate candidates (email, phone, contact email, name), safe merge (children moved, loser kept as `merged` with snapshot in `a056_merge_log`, loser opt-outs carried to survivor, cross-business merge refused).
- **Consent**: append-only events per channel/purpose; no consent => no send; opt-out creates a suppression keyed by customer and hashed address that wins over any later grant (also across duplicate records) until an authorised, audited lift; marketing opt-out does not block service messages, service opt-out blocks both. Public-intake consent is only a *claim* applied after staff triage and never overrides opt-out.
- **Campaigns**: provider-neutral **NO-OP** only (`provider='NOOP'`, `sent` always 0, statuses `NOOP_NOT_SENT`/`BLOCKED_NOT_SENT`). Real SMS/e-mail/WhatsApp activation is NOT ENABLED.
- **Intake**: per-endpoint token (only sha256 stored, shown once), rate limit, idempotency key, strict payload whitelist/size cap. Public requests become `RECEIVED` (or `DRAFT` for order requests) enquiries; no order, stock, payment or refund is ever created. Return/refund requests are tickets only.
- **Privacy**: export package, CSV export with formula-injection neutralisation (`a056_csv_cell`), owner-only redaction that clears PII everywhere, blocks while work is open, keeps hashed suppressions. HTML is stored inert; renderers must escape (`core10-crm-lifecycle-engine.js` `escapeHtml`).
- **Reports**: counts come from CRM records; money from quotes is advisory; rates are `null` (not 0) when the denominator is 0. Retention/repeat use A049 `posted` status; the purchase date is the CRM order-link date because the A049 overview exposes no posted date (labelled in the response).

## Isolated test adapter
`a056_test_adapter_create_order_v1` (recorded `adapter='TEST_ADAPTER'`, no A049 order, fulfilment always `unavailable`) works only when the A049 contract is absent or simulated absent (`a056.simulate_a049_missing=on`) on a disposable database; otherwise it raises `A056_USE_CANONICAL_ADAPTER`. `a056_test_finance_*` functions exist only inside the test file to exercise the finance registry.

## JS
`core10-crm-lifecycle-client.js` (signed RPC wrappers with arg validation, error-code extraction, public intake, HMAC envelope helpers) and `core10-crm-lifecycle-engine.js` (pure BigInt money/quote maths, consent/SLA/funnel/segment logic, escaping). Node tests in `tests/c10_a056_{client,engine}.test.js`; the client test also checks SQL/contract name sync.

## Known gaps / not claimed
Not tested against GoTrue or production Supabase; no certified finance read model (A022 is funding-only); no loyalty points ledger (config only); no real notification provider; no booking engine; business-hours SLA calendars are not implemented (calendar hours); site-tier uses A018 site grants; A049 overview gives no posted timestamp. Root `AGENTS.md` fails the inherited `forbidden_files` check from the Preview V1 base; A056 files add no offenders.
